channel_id.description: ChannelID shares the link in a campaign channel: the destination gets its utm_source, utm_medium and utm_campaign.

verification.description: Verification is the DNS record to create; it is left out once the domain is verified.

campaign_name.description: CampaignName and ChannelName name them, so a list of links needs no other request; empty when the link is outside every campaign.

qr_style.description: QRStyle is how the link's QR code is drawn; null fields are the default (black, white, no logo).

get.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

post.description: A campaign groups links by marketing initiative; add channels to it, then put links in the channels. The name is unique in the organization, ignoring case. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.

delete.description: Removes the campaign and its channels. Its links stay, outside every campaign, and keep the UTM parameters they already carry. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.

get.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

patch.description: Links already in the campaign keep the utm_campaign they were given; a new name only reaches the links put in its channels afterwards. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.

get.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.
get.summary: List the channels of a campaign

post.description: A channel is a place the campaign is shared (Instagram, email...). Its name becomes the utm_source of the links put in it, so it is unique in the campaign, ignoring case. A campaign has at most 100 channels. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.
post.summary: Add a channel to a campaign

delete.description: Its links stay, outside every campaign, and keep the UTM parameters they already carry. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.
delete.summary: Delete a channel of a campaign

get.description: A CSV file with one row per link of the campaign: link_id, short_url, origin_url, channel, clicks and created_at. clicks counts the clicks between from and to (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC, both included); without them it counts every click. Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

Clicks of all the links in the campaign's channels per day, hour, weekday, referrer, country and device, plus the clicks of each channel, between from and to, the total of the previous period of the same length, optionally narrowed to one country, device or referrer. Without dates it covers the last 30 days. Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

get.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

parameters.description: Only links in a channel of this campaign
parameters.name: campaign_id

post.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope. alias, expires_at, max_clicks, password, domain_id and channel_id are optional. With a channel_id the destination gets utm_source (the channel), utm_medium=useshortly and utm_campaign (the campaign), replacing those parameters if it already had them.

delete.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.

get.description: Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

put.description: Rewrites the destination with the utm_source (the channel), utm_medium=useshortly and utm_campaign (the campaign) of the channel, replacing those parameters if the link already had them. A missing or null channel_id takes the link out of its campaign and removes those three parameters from the destination. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.
put.summary: Put a link in a campaign channel

get.description: An image of the short URL, not JSON, drawn with the link's QR colors (the logo is not drawn by the server). Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.

put.description: Colors are #rrggbb, the foreground darker than the background with enough contrast to scan. logo_url is an https image that clients draw in the middle of the code; the server only stores it. Missing fields are reset to the default. Needs a JWT or an API key with the write scope.

get.description: Clicks per day, hour, weekday, referrer, country and device between from and to, the total of the previous period of the same length, optionally narrowed to one country, device or referrer. Without dates it covers the last 30 days. Needs a JWT or an API key with the read scope.
